claude.sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

links.outcome: Whether human expert verification of AI outputs caught errors versus a fully autonomous AI workflow
links.effect: S-ACAD with 19 human interventions: no critical safety errors found by 2 external specialists; F-ACAD without human review produced 17 issues (9 high-priority). Expert changed AI-generated diazepam pathway to require calling 911. Single case.
links.quote: Although F-ACAD reviewed more sources and produced a more complex algorithm, its own AI critics identified 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns related to US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and parent-friendly communication.

links.outcome: Whether clinician review/approval of AI-drafted clinical content prevented errors reaching final output
links.effect: Expert-in-the-loop version had no medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors per 2 reviewers (validity 9.0 and 9.5/10); fully automated version had 17 issues (9 high-priority). Single expert, single topic, no independent coding.
links.quote: Crucially, neither reviewer independently identified medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction.

links.outcome: Independent external specialist review of AI-assisted algorithm for critical safety errors
links.effect: Two independent board-certified pediatric specialists found no critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction; rated clinical validity 9.0 and 9.5/10; reviewer A scored 3/5 on practical executability of one item.
links.quote: This review served as a vital safety check against potential oversights by the single developer.

links.outcome: Independent clinician review of AI-generated clinical content before deployment
links.effect: External pediatric emergency physician and pediatrician reviewed the algorithm; none identified critical safety errors; both rated it usable after minor revisions, pending usability testing.
links.quote: Neither reviewer identified critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction, providing some reassurance that execution bias did not compromise clinical safety in this single-case run.

links.outcome: Comparison of human-checkpointed workflow versus fully autonomous multi-agent workflow on quality issues
links.effect: Fully autonomous 14-agent system finished in ~68 min vs 245 min but its critics flagged 17 issues (9 high, 8 medium); human-in-loop version had 19 interventions and no critical safety errors identified by external review.
links.quote: However, this substantial reduction in time was accompanied by notable quality trade-offs.

links.outcome: Whether AI critic (AI sparring) surfaced gaps in AI drafts for expert scrutiny
links.effect: Claude critic identified 16 improvement suggestions for the Gemini draft; 14 (88%) adopted after expert review (logic gaps 3/3, UX 5/7, missing scenarios 4/4, safety 2/2).
links.quote: Of these, 14 (88%) were adopted into the final algorithm after expert review.

links.outcome: Hallucination-like clinical content errors in AI-generated guidance
links.effect: AI initially generated a protocol letting parents give diazepam after 5 minutes of seizure; expert modified it to require calling 911 first. Autonomous system's critics found 17 issues incl. 9 high-priority.
links.quote: The human expert intervened to modify this pathway, mandating that parents call 911 for real-time instructions before administration ( Multimedia Appendix 4 ).

unlisted_practices: Multi-LLM drafter-critic ('AI sparring') cross-check of AI-generated clinical content
Parallel multi-model data collection to reduce single-model bias
Evidence-level tagging of each recommendation in AI-assisted guidance

links.outcome: independent clinical review findings
links.effect: Two independent pediatric specialists found no medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors; clinical validity ratings were 9.0/10 and 9.5/10.
links.quote: Crucially, neither reviewer independently identified medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction.

links.outcome: clinician verification of AI outputs
links.effect: S-ACAD used 19 human interventions; clinical judgment 8/19 (42%) and safety review 5/19 (26%). F-ACAD generated 17 issues, 9 high priority.
links.quote: During the workflow, 19 human expert interventions were recorded, with clinical judgment (n=8, 42.1%) and safety review (n=5, 26.3%) as the most frequent categories in an exploratory post hoc analysis.

links.outcome: safety-critical override of AI draft
links.effect: One safety-critical override changed AI’s direct diazepam pathway to require calling 911; 19 total human expert interventions were logged.
links.quote: The human expert intervened to modify this pathway, mandating that parents call 911 for real-time instructions before administration ( Multimedia Appendix 4 ).

links.outcome: domain-expert governance versus automation
links.effect: Expert-governed S-ACAD had no mandatory critical safety corrections; fully automated F-ACAD was 3.6× faster but generated 17 issues, 9 high priority.
links.quote: The fully automated comparator (F-ACAD), although approximately 3.6 times faster, generated 17 issues (9 high priority) that overlapped with the categories in which human oversight was concentrated in S-ACAD.

links.outcome: standard-of-care and emergency-response errors
links.effect: F-ACAD had 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns about US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and communication.
links.quote: Although F-ACAD reviewed more sources and produced a more complex algorithm, its own AI critics identified 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns related to US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and parent-friendly communication.

unlisted_practices: Parallel multimodel querying (“LLM Council”) to surface disagreements and reduce single-model bias
AI sparring with a second LLM critic to identify logic, usability, missing-scenario, and safety improvements
Evidence-level tagging of each parent-facing clinical action guideline
Benchmarking a human-in-the-loop workflow against a fully autonomous multiagent content-development baseline

links.outcome: Independent expert evaluation of clinical accuracy, safety, and validity
links.effect: Two independent pediatric specialists identified no medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction, and rated clinical validity 9.0 and 9.5 out of 10.
links.quote: Two independent pediatric specialists (N=2) reviewed the output and did not identify medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction, and both rated overall clinical validity highly (9.0 and 9.5 out of 10).

links.outcome: Adoption of AI-critique suggestions surfacing gaps for expert review
links.effect: AI critic identified 16 improvement suggestions (logic gaps, UX, missing scenarios, safety), of which 14 (88%) were adopted into the final algorithm after expert review.
links.quote: The high adoption rate (14/16, 88%) indicates that AI-generated critiques were frequently incorporated after expert review, which may reflect the mechanism’s capacity to challenge and refine initial decisions.

unlisted_practices: Parallel multi-model data collection (LLM council) to mitigate single-model bias
Semiautomatic clinical algorithm development (S-ACAD) framework combining AI drafting with iterative expert oversight
